A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods and experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on reward shaping, option discovery, count-based exploration and transfer learning in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix C, including learning curves, visitation analyses and numerical comparisons.

M1.justification: The DR formulations, dynamic-programming and TD updates, default features, and RACE algorithm are unchanged. The maximum-entropy representation is retained in Appendix B.5 after moving from Section 5.2; expanded explanations do not introduce new procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same grid environments, constant-reward variants, larger grid environments, RiverSwim, SixArms and multiple-goal transfer setting. No datasets, tasks or evaluation scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: SR-based and unshaped reward shaping; CEO, random walk and Q-learning variants; Sarsa and Sarsa+SR; and successor features with the same policy counts. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training budgets, hyperparameter grids, reward preprocessing and transfer reward sampling remain unchanged, including Tables 2–3 and Appendix C. The precomputed-eigenvector assumption and lambda-selection explanation add documentation without establishing changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: The constant-reward controls, exploration learning curves and state-visitation heatmaps in Figures 6–9 are retained. No new ablations, robustness tests or supplementary empirical analyses are reported; the added numerical-stability discussion explains implementation choices.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same run counts, individual-seed displays and 95% confidence intervals. Appendix D preserves the same normal-approximation formula and explanation of randomness across runs.

E6.justification: The experimental figure images and Table 1 results are unchanged. For example, Sarsa+DR still obtains 2,964 and 3,518 in thousands on RiverSwim and SixArms, respectively. The reported performance rankings and comparative findings are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 now requires constant negative rewards and gamma in (0,1), and restricts the ordered-eigenvector equivalence to symmetric SR and DR matrices. Appendix B.2 replaces the brief ordering assertion with a substantive proof using derivatives, Gershgorin bounds and exclusion of a vertical asymptote. These changes repair the scope and justification of a central theoretical result.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion stop listing the maximum-entropy extension as a main contribution, concentrating their contribution summaries on DR learning, eigenspectrum analysis and default features. The MER itself remains in Appendix B.5, and the abstract and principal empirical claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains why non-terminal reward changes invalidate reuse of default features, identifies possible numerical difficulties over long horizons, and recommends considering SR when rewards are constant. It also explicitly acknowledges the reward-shaping experiments' reliance on precomputed eigenvectors. These refine limitations already partly discussed in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds a paper-specific code link. Appendix C.1 explains that lambda was increased from 1 in increments of 0.1 to select the already-used value 1.3 alongside python-flint. Section 6.1 explicitly documents access to eigenvectors before policy training; this is additional disclosure, not evidence of changed implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds context on zero-shot RL and other proto-representations, credits Ringstrom et al. for the preceding state-action formulation of linearly solvable MDPs, attributes the SR trajectory identity to Blier et al., and notes a connection to relative entropy policy search. These are targeted attribution and positioning improvements; the main related-work argument remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 expands explanations of eigenoptions, default-feature transfer and limitations, clarifies notation, and makes small language corrections. It moves the MER discussion from Section 5.2 into Appendix B.5 and simplifies Section 5's structure. Most prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All ten figures and three tables are retained with unchanged graphics and table contents. Appendix displays are rearranged, particularly Table 2 and Figures 7–10, and Figure 5 receives a small caption clarification. There are no new or redrawn result displays.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper through a better-qualified Theorem 3.1 and a substantive justification of eigenvalue ordering, more accurate prior-work attribution, and clearer applicability and implementation information. These focused improvements increase rigor and reproducibility while preserving the original methods, experimental evidence and relocated MER content.
